you want player-friendly seasonal progression systems

citations.review_text:
Quick to pick up, fast rounds, COOP PVE and runs very well at 1440p with a GTX 1060 6GB and an i7 7700.

A perfect game to have fun with your mates from time to time, even with that one friend who has not upgraded his pc in 10 years.

very good multi player game. get drunk, dance to the jukebox, do a mission, shoot eachother in said mission, get better guns and upgrades, repeat. very fun loop and gunplay. peak voicelines as well. it also runs on a potato, as you can see (i get 45fps 1200p ultra) 8.5/10, would recommend if you are even remotely interested in multiplayer shooters with friends.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe season passes as free with no fear of missing out, allowing players to revisit past seasons and events.

citations.review_text:
One of the best co-op games out there, with one of the most friendly communities to boot, everyone is helpful towards new players.
There are also no progression-affecting microtransactions, and cosmetics purchasable with real money are not shoved in your face, despite the game being in continuous development; seasons and season passes are available for free, and can be revisited any time, without any FOMO bs. I wish more game developers respected their players half as much as GSG does.

Sure, the gameplay is fun. But what makes it the greatest multiplayer game for me is the fact that it has all the addicting features of modern multiplayers, but does not capitalize on them: There is a season pass, but it's free. There are season-exclusive cosmetics, but you can always switch to a previous season to get the unlocks you want. There are yearly time-limited events with exclusive cosmetics, but every year you can unlock the cosmetics from previous iterations of the event. The fun of unlocking cosmetics, but without the FOMO.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game runs well and performs smoothly on lower-end hardware.

citations.review_text: Tons of fun to play with a friend. Great atmosphere, easy to jump in and play for 20 mins, or hours. Runs great on lower-end systems. Kid-friendly too. Totally awesome.

I have about 500 hours on the Xbox Game Pass version of the game. Since it was leaving GP, I had to finally pay some money because they definitely deserve it. Save transfer was very easy and all my unlocks and levels and perks/guns/etc transferred. Many achievements did, but not all. Some, I'm finding, unlock once you level one thing in that category (upgrading bosco for example, I just had to interact with the station).

I'm pretty excited to buy the DLC as well. Until late 2025 I played it on a GTX 1080 on a 32:9 super ultrawide with settings maxed without issue. Idk 300+ fps? Sometimes it'd chunk on heavier stuff but this game runs flawlessly on low hardware. Looks great with DLAA now that I've got the steam version.

It's just fun. Everyone is chill. Loot is all shared. We all work together. Perks and builds are fun. PvE done right.

Rock and Stone!

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the battle passes and seasonal progression as free, allowing players to earn rewards through gameplay without utilizing FOMO tactics.

citations.review_text: No Constantly updated. Can pick whatever battle pass you want to grind for, for free. Lots of customisation to build out your class. Challenging missions. Endless replayability.

This game has so much good to it's genuinely difficult to type a review but I want to give it my best attempt. 
As somebody who plays a lot of competitive games (e.g Overwatch and Left 4 Dead 2) this game is amazing to come back to as a great chill experience, super low cortisol gameplay. Its quite easy to pick up and play with a great Tutorial that doesn't take too long and things like Upgrades for your equipment being introduced slowly to allow players to get a great grasp of the game. 
The Gameplay Loops are super engaging, these include Second to Second loops such as; finding minerals and mining them then Depositing them, aiming at a bug shooting them and then eliminating them (keeping PG). Then there are the Minute to Minute loops; exploring a cave for all of its resources, dong the particular objective like building a pipeline, escorting a drill dozer moving an Aquarqs stuff like that. The Mission loop of Dropping in doing the objective then getting out. And of course the over arching gameplay loops of leveling up your dwarves maxing the level then doing their promotion assignment then promoting them changing their portrait and starting back at level 1. 
All of these Gameplay Loops create an incredible experience that I think can be enjoyed by everyone. 
The game is surprisingly cheap goes on sale quite often has no predatory micro transactions all the battle passes are free and you earn all the rewards by playing the game and finding crates and lost dwarves throughout some missions. 
I Hugely recommend this game for everyone no critiques 10/10.

Incredible variation between runs. Lots of weird synergies to discover with the overclock system. Challenges aplenty if one wants it. I also love that every class feels different and brings something unique to the table.

Last but not least, thanks for the devs for not use FOMO tactics. It's really great to see someone doing it this way, as in seasonal cosmetics and content is accessible all the way to the beginning for anyone. I gladly buy cosmetic DLCs just to support dev decisions that respect the players.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that cave generation provides vast, varied, complex, and procedurally generated environments that remain unpredictable across runs.

citations.review_text:
simply the very best that co-op shooters have to offer.

Deep Rock Galactic offers a brilliant blend of spelunking and combat. missions are all well paced(except for industrial sabotage), each class feels distinct and offers a unique roll to fill for the team, both in and out of combat. some will be better at certain thing than others so it's important to help your fellow dwarf out. enemy variety is vast but balanced in a way that' doesn't feel overpowering to deal with. Cave generation is vast, varied, complex, and often dangerous. to aid variety is the biomes, each has their own color palette, environmental hazards, and even enemies. you'll go a long time before seeing the same layout twice and each cave system is a delight to explore. 

Customization plays a major role in deepening the experience. each dwarf can customize their kit with different weapons, mods and overclocks to change how your class performs in combat. There's also loads of cosmetic customization, from armors, moustaches and beards, and even pickaxe parts. 

topping off this great game is general atmosphere and vibes. it's easy to just hop into a match and have a good time with your teammates. and it's backed up with years of content updates, with more on the horizon. grab some friends and have a blast!
Best procedural generation I saw in a game.

single_points.text: One reviewer notes that the overclocks distribution in the late game is pretty much pure rng, so it may take quite a while if you want a specific overclock for your build.

citation.review_text:
probably one of the best coop horde shooters out there, definitely the best iteration of a live service gameto ever exist, there is genuinely very little to criticise, everything in the game has a purpose, the lore is surprisingly deep and allows for a lot of lore-crafting, impeccable gameplay experience, very well balanced difficulty system, a lot of progression options, absolutely WONDERFUL music and an artstyle that grows on you and reveals its beauty if you just give it a chance. 

the only thing to criticise would be the overclocks distribution in the late game - is pretty much pure rng, so it may take quite a while if you want a specific overclock for your build. overall not too serious, but does dampen the excitement a bit after a while. 

developers are very friendly and very active in their own community, taking close care of it and interacting with it a lot, even doing weekly streams, too! 
community is very healthy overall, in my 200h i only ever had 1 bad experience and it wasn't even for long. if anything, the community is very welcoming and almost too excited over any new greenbeards to help and play with.

Rock and Stone, miners, see you on the job!
